Aloevera.properties: Bitter, sweet; cooling, heavy; balances Pitta
Aloevera.uses: Burns, skin irritation, constipation, digestion, hair and scalp care
Aloevera.how: Fresh leaf gel on burns, skin and scalp; gel juice for digestion; used in Kumaryasava
Aloevera.caution: The yellow latex is a strong laxative; avoid in pregnancy.

Amla.properties: Sour with most tastes (not salty); cooling; balances all three doshas; a Rasayana (rejuvenator)
Amla.uses: Immunity, digestion, eye and hair health; rich in vitamin C
Amla.how: Fruit eaten fresh, dried or as churna; key ingredient of Chyawanprash and Triphala
Amla.caution: May increase acidity in some people; check with a doctor if on diabetes medicine.

Amruthaballi.properties: Bitter, astringent; heating; balances all three doshas, mainly Pitta
Amruthaballi.uses: Chronic fever, immunity, diabetes support, joint pain, liver support
Amruthaballi.how: Stem juice or decoction (Guduchi kashayam); Guduchi satva; Amritarishta
Amruthaballi.caution: Avoid in autoimmune disease and pregnancy; may lower blood sugar.

Arali.properties: Astringent, sweet; cooling; balances Kapha and Pitta
Arali.uses: Skin problems, diarrhea, wound healing, asthma and diabetes (traditional)
Arali.how: Bark is part of Panchavalkala decoction for washing wounds; leaf and bark decoctions
Arali.caution: May lower blood sugar. Traditional use.

Astma_weed.uses: Asthma, cough, bronchitis, dysentery, wound healing
Astma_weed.how: Whole-plant decoction or juice in folk medicine for cough and bowel complaints
Astma_weed.caution: The latex irritates skin and eyes; use under guidance; avoid in pregnancy.

Badipala.uses: Information is not shown because the dataset gives no botanical name for this label
Badipala.caution: Identify the species with a botanist before any use.

Balloon_Vine.uses: Joint pain, arthritis, stiffness, earache, skin conditions
Balloon_Vine.how: Leaf paste or medicated oil on painful joints; leaves in dosa and soup (Mudakathan) in South India
Balloon_Vine.caution: Mostly external use; avoid in pregnancy.

Bamboo.uses: Cough, weakness, fever; bamboo manna is valued for lung health
Bamboo.how: Vamsha lochana (bamboo manna) in Sitopaladi and Talisadi churna; leaf decoction in folk use

Beans.uses: Nutrition (protein, fibre); pod decoction in folk use for urinary and blood sugar complaints
Beans.how: Pods and seeds cooked in the daily diet
Beans.caution: Raw beans are toxic; cook well.

Betel.properties: Pungent, bitter; heating; balances Kapha and Vata
Betel.how: Leaf chewed after meals; warmed leaf on the chest for cough and on boils
Betel.caution: Chewing with tobacco or areca nut is linked to oral cancer.

Bhrami.properties: Bitter, astringent; cooling; balances Pitta and Vata; a brain tonic (Medhya)
Bhrami.uses: Memory, focus, anxiety, stress; epilepsy support (traditional)
Bhrami.how: Leaf juice or powder; Brahmi ghrita; Brahmi vati
Bhrami.caution: May cause stomach upset; caution with thyroid or sedative medicines.

Bringaraja.properties: Bitter, pungent; heating; balances Kapha and Vata
Bringaraja.uses: Hair fall, premature greying, liver support, skin
Bringaraja.how: Leaf juice or Bhringaraja taila (oil) on the scalp; leaf juice with honey
Bringaraja.caution: Use the oil externally; rare allergies.

Caricature.uses: Folk use for constipation, hemorrhoids, wounds and ulcers
Caricature.how: Leaf juice or paste in folk practice
Caricature.caution: Very limited evidence; use under guidance.

Castor.properties: Sweet, pungent; heating; balances Vata and Kapha
Castor.how: Warm leaves tied on painful joints; castor oil as a purgative and in Eranda taila
Castor.caution: Seeds are highly poisonous; castor oil is not for use in pregnancy.

Catharanthus.uses: Source of vinca alkaloids used in cancer drugs; folk use for diabetes
Catharanthus.how: Leaf or flower decoction in folk medicine
Catharanthus.caution: Toxic if self-medicated; never replace diabetes or cancer treatment.

Chakte.uses: Information is not shown because the dataset gives no botanical name for this label
Chakte.caution: Identify the species with a botanist before any use.

Chilly.how: Used in food; capsaicin creams and rubs on joints and muscles
Chilly.caution: Irritates stomach and skin; avoid in ulcers and acidity.

Citron lime (herelikai).properties: Sour, sweet; digestive; balances Vata and Kapha
Citron lime (herelikai).uses: Indigestion, nausea, loss of appetite, cough
Citron lime (herelikai).how: Fruit juice, rind and pickle; Matulunga preparations

Coffee.how: Mainly the seed (coffee) as a drink; leaves are made into tea in some regions
Coffee.caution: Caffeine: avoid in anxiety and heart rhythm problems; limit in pregnancy.

Common rue(naagdalli).uses: Colic, menstrual complaints, muscle spasm, earache (traditional)
Common rue(naagdalli).how: Small amounts of leaf infusion; leaf in folk remedies for children's colic
Common rue(naagdalli).caution: Toxic in larger doses; avoid in pregnancy; sap can burn skin in sunlight.

Coriender.properties: Sweet, bitter, pungent; cooling; balances all doshas
Coriender.uses: Digestion, burning sensation, urinary comfort, allergy
Coriender.how: Leaves in food; seeds as cold infusion (Dhanyaka hima) or decoction

Curry.uses: Digestion, nausea, hair health; folk use for blood sugar
Curry.how: Leaves in tempering, chutney and buttermilk; leaf paste for hair

Doddpathre.uses: Cough, cold, sore throat, indigestion, kidney stones (folk)
Doddpathre.how: Leaf juice with honey for children's cough; leaf fritters

Drumstick.properties: Pungent, bitter; heating; balances Kapha and Vata
Drumstick.uses: Nutrition (iron, vitamins), inflammation, joint pain, lactation support
Drumstick.how: Leaves in curries and powder; pods in sambar; bark and root only under guidance
Drumstick.caution: Root and bark are unsafe in pregnancy.

Ekka.uses: Skin diseases, joint pain, swelling, thorn removal
Ekka.how: Leaves warmed on joints; latex externally; internal use only after purification by an expert
Ekka.caution: The latex is toxic and harms eyes; never take it on your own.

Eucalyptus.uses: Cold, blocked nose, sinusitis, cough, muscle pain
Eucalyptus.how: Leaf steam inhalation; eucalyptus oil in balms
Eucalyptus.caution: The oil is toxic if swallowed; not for infants' faces.

Ganike.properties: Bitter, pungent; reduces all three doshas (traditional)
Ganike.uses: Mouth and stomach ulcers, liver complaints, jaundice, fever
Ganike.how: Tender leaves cooked as greens (Ganike soppu / Manathakkali keerai); leaf juice
Ganike.caution: The raw plant and unripe berries are toxic; eat only the cooked leaves.

Gasagase.uses: Seeds used as food, in cooling drinks and for sleep and cough
Gasagase.how: Seeds (khus khus) in curries, sweets and Ayurvedic preparations
Gasagase.caution: The latex (opium) is a controlled drug; growing the plant is restricted in India under the NDPS Act.

Ginger.properties: Pungent; heating; balances Vata and Kapha
Ginger.uses: Indigestion, nausea, cough and cold, joint pain
Ginger.how: Fresh juice with honey; dry ginger in Trikatu and kashayams
Ginger.caution: May thin blood; avoid large amounts in pregnancy and with blood thinners.

Globe Amarnath.uses: Folk use of flowers for cough, bronchitis and urinary complaints
Globe Amarnath.how: Flower tea or decoction in folk practice

Guava.uses: Diarrhea, mouth ulcers, gum health, toothache
Guava.how: Tender leaves chewed or boiled as a gargle; leaf tea
Guava.caution: Leaf extracts may lower blood sugar.

Henna.uses: Hair conditioning, skin cooling, burns, wounds, headache
Henna.how: Leaf paste on hair, palms, soles and burns; leaf decoction as a gargle
Henna.caution: Patch test for allergy; avoid black henna dyes.

Hibiscus.uses: Hair fall, scalp care, heavy menstrual bleeding (traditional)
Hibiscus.how: Flower and leaf paste or oil on the scalp; flower tea

Honge.how: Seed oil (Karanja taila) externally; leaf paste or decoction for skin washes
Honge.caution: Seed oil is for external use only.

Insulin.uses: Eaten traditionally for blood sugar control
Insulin.how: One or two fresh leaves chewed daily in folk practice
Insulin.caution: Can add to diabetes medicines; never stop prescribed treatment.

Jackfruit.uses: Mouth ulcers and diarrhea (leaves, traditional); fruit as food
Jackfruit.how: Leaf decoction as a gargle; fruit and seeds cooked
Jackfruit.caution: Heavy to digest; limit in diabetes.

Jasmine.uses: Mouth ulcers, skin problems, wounds, headache
Jasmine.how: Leaves chewed or boiled for mouth ulcers; Jatyadi taila for wounds; flower oil

Kambajala.how: Flower tea; root and leaf decoction in folk and Ayurvedic use

Kasambruga.uses: Information is not shown because the dataset gives no botanical name for this label
Kasambruga.caution: Identify the species with a botanist before any use.

Kohlrabi.uses: Mainly a food: vitamin C, fibre, digestion
Kohlrabi.caution: Large amounts can affect the thyroid in sensitive people.

Lantana.uses: Folk use for cuts, itching, rheumatism, fever
Lantana.how: Leaf paste or steam applied externally
Lantana.caution: Leaves and unripe berries are toxic if eaten; external use only.

Lemon.properties: Sour; heating; balances Vata and Kapha
Lemon.uses: Digestion, nausea, cold, scurvy, throat comfort
Lemon.how: Juice in warm water with honey; rind in pickles
Lemon.caution: Excess harms tooth enamel and may cause acidity.

Malabar_Nut.properties: Bitter, astringent; cooling; balances Kapha and Pitta
Malabar_Nut.how: Leaf juice with honey; Vasarishta and Vasavaleha

Malabar_Spinach.how: Leaves cooked as greens; leaf juice
Malabar_Spinach.caution: Rich in oxalates: caution with kidney stones.

Mango.uses: Diarrhea, mouth and throat problems, dental care
Mango.how: Tender leaves chewed to clean teeth; leaf decoction as a gargle; bark decoction

Marigold.uses: Wounds, skin infections, earache, eye care (traditional)
Marigold.how: Flower or leaf paste on wounds; flower juice as ear drops in folk use
Marigold.caution: Allergy risk in people sensitive to daisy-family plants.

Mint.how: Leaf chutney, tea and digestive drinks

Neem.properties: Bitter, astringent; cooling; balances Pitta and Kapha
Neem.uses: Skin disorders, acne, blood purification, dental care, worms
Neem.how: Leaf paste and baths; twigs as toothbrush (datun); neem oil
Neem.caution: Avoid in pregnancy and in infants.

Nelavembu.how: Whole-plant decoction; Nilavembu kashayam in Siddha medicine, widely used in fevers
Nelavembu.caution: Avoid in pregnancy; may lower blood pressure.

Nerale.how: Seed powder; fruit; leaf and bark decoction as a gargle or wash

Nooni.how: Fruit juice; leaf poultice on joints
Nooni.caution: Caution in kidney or liver disease; high in potassium.

Onion.uses: Cold, digestion, insect bites, heart health (traditional)
Onion.how: Juice with honey for cough; raw or cooked in food

Padri.uses: Limited reliable information; traditional use of bark and root for fever and inflammation

Palak(Spinach).how: Leaves cooked as greens and soups
Palak(Spinach).caution: Rich in oxalates; caution with kidney stones and blood thinners.

Papaya.uses: Digestion, skin, wounds; leaf juice used in folk medicine for fever
Papaya.how: Ripe fruit; raw papain on wounds; leaf juice only under medical advice
Papaya.caution: Avoid unripe fruit and latex in pregnancy.

Parijatha.how: Leaf juice or decoction; leaf juice with honey for fever

Pepper.properties: Pungent; heating; balances Kapha and Vata
Pepper.how: In Trikatu; kashayam with tulsi and ginger; with honey
Pepper.caution: Avoid excess in acidity and pregnancy.

Pomoegranate.how: Fruit juice; rind decoction for dysentery; leaf decoction
Pomoegranate.caution: May interact with some blood pressure medicines.

Pumpkin.how: Leaves and fruit cooked; Kushmanda preparations; seeds for worms in folk use

Sapota.uses: Energy, digestion; bark and leaf in folk use for fever and diarrhea
Sapota.how: Ripe fruit; bark decoction in folk use
Sapota.caution: Do not eat the seeds; may raise blood sugar.

Seethaashoka.uses: Information is not shown because the dataset gives no botanical name for this label
Seethaashoka.caution: Identify the species with a botanist before any use.

Seethapala.uses: Fruit as food; leaf paste on boils and for lice in folk use
Seethapala.caution: Seeds and leaves are toxic if eaten; avoid contact with eyes.

Tamarind.uses: Digestion, mild laxative, fever, joint swelling
Tamarind.how: Pulp in rasam; leaf poultice on swelling

Taro.uses: Nutrition and digestion; leaves used in food
Taro.caution: Never eat raw; it causes itching and throat irritation.

Tecoma.uses: Folk use for blood sugar and digestive complaints
Tecoma.caution: Limited evidence; may lower blood sugar.

Thumbe.uses: Cold, cough, headache, fever, skin complaints
Thumbe.how: Leaf juice drops in the nose for headache and sinus in folk use; leaves in chutney

Tomato.how: Fruit eaten raw or cooked; juice

Tulsi.properties: Pungent, bitter; heating; balances Kapha and Vata
Tulsi.uses: Cough, cold, fever, asthma support, stress
Tulsi.how: Leaf juice with honey; kashayam with ginger and pepper; chewed leaves
Tulsi.caution: May lower blood sugar; avoid high doses in pregnancy.

Turmeric.properties: Bitter, pungent; heating; balances Kapha and Pitta
Turmeric.uses: Wound healing, inflammation, skin conditions, liver support
Turmeric.how: Rhizome powder with warm milk; paste on wounds; leaves in steamed dishes
Turmeric.caution: High doses affect gallstones and blood thinners.

ashoka.uses: Heavy menstrual bleeding, uterine disorders, pain
ashoka.caution: Use under guidance; beware of look-alike false ashoka sold as the herb.

camphor.how: Camphor in balms and steam inhalation
camphor.caution: Toxic if swallowed; keep away from children.

kamakasturi.uses: Digestion, cough, cold; seeds (sabja) are cooling
kamakasturi.how: Leaf tea; soaked seeds in cooling drinks

kepala.how: Flower or leaf decoction in folk practice

Ganigale.how: Leaves warmed on joints; latex externally; internal use only after purification by an expert
